method.categories: Hello world, Database and Application are throughput categories; Memory and Startup are costs scored as Axum's value / the implementation's; Stability (Tiers 2 and 4) is a pass, warn or fail check without a score
method.ratios: medians of the per-round ratios to Axum measured on the same runner, pooled over every job (runner) of an implementation; each throughput run counts with its capacity ratio: the requests/s ratio, or, when either side was client-bound, the CPU-cost ratio (requests per CPU-second of the server and PostgreSQL together); a side limited by the load generator while its server used less than 75% of its vCPUs makes that round pair not comparable
method.limits: a run is client-bound when the vCPUs the load generator and PostgreSQL share were at least 90% busy; it is PostgreSQL-bound when PostgreSQL used more of them than the load generator, and load-generator-bound otherwise
method.floors: Memory counts every high-water mark as at least 64 MiB and Startup every time as at least 1 s, so that differences far below what matters in production do not move the scores
method.ties: two scores tie when their gap in natural-log units is at most the largest of (a) the A/A margin (the largest deviation from 1.00 of the A/A control's scores, per job and pooled), (b) the root of the sum of squares of the two implementations' between-job spreads (the half-range of the logarithms of their per-job scores) and (c) the pooled floor (the median spread of the ranked implementations measured on at least two jobs); an implementation whose jobs all ran on one CPU model counts with at least the floor as its spread, one measured on a single job with the floor, and each run in which most round pairs had one side PostgreSQL-bound and the other not adds the change in CPU cost with the load measured for its endpoint (README, CPU split: 7% for single-query reads, 2% for /fortunes, a third for /queries and the writes) divided by the category's number of runs to the spread (root of the sum of squares); the scores are sorted and a new group starts only where two neighbouring scores are further apart than their margin, so neighbours within their margin always share a group, and every member gets the range of positions the group occupies; a score within max(a, its spread, c) of 1.00 is marked as indistinguishable from Axum; in Startup, neighbouring times within the readiness poll interval also share a group
method.not comparable: a run whose round pairs were mostly not comparable (see ratios) has no score in its category
method.errors: a run whose median error rate is above 1% (any response that is not 2xx, any transport error or timeout) has no score in its category; the cell shows the error rate
method.incomplete: an implementation without a value for every run of a category (not measured, not served according to its bench.json "endpoints", or left out by a correction) has no position in it
method.roles: Axum is the reference (1.00); diagnostics (for example Rullst's minimal configuration) and the A/A control are listed next to it, with a score and without a position
method.overall: the weighted geometric mean of the five category scores (config.json scoring.overall_weights: Hello world, Database and Application twice, Memory and Startup once, because the Memory and Startup floors make most native implementations tie there), with the same tie margins and position ranges; published when config.json scoring.publish_overall is true, with a sensitivity table of the positions under other weightings, equal weights included; the categories are the result, the overall score a summary for quick reading
